Global (All).title: US-Iran Tensions Escalate Amid Reports of New Drone Attack
Global (All).summary: The US and Iran are on high alert after reports of a new drone attack on Iranian soil. The incident has raised tensions between the two nations and has sparked concerns about a potential military conflict.

Global (All).title: Ukraine War: Russian Strikes Hit Key Infrastructure
Global (All).summary: Russian forces have launched a series of strikes on key infrastructure targets in Ukraine, including power plants and transportation hubs. The attacks have caused widespread damage and have disrupted critical services.

Global (All).title: Global Cyber Attack Hits Major Companies
Global (All).summary: A global cyber attack has hit several major companies, including a UK-based energy firm and a US-based tech giant. The attack is believed to be the work of a state-sponsored hacking group and has raised concerns about the vulnerability of critical infrastructure.

United States.title: US Supreme Court to hear Biden administration bid to reinstate Trump-era "Remain in Mexico" policy.
United States.summary: The US Supreme Court has agreed to hear the Biden administration's appeal of a federal court ruling that reinstated a Trump-era policy forcing thousands of migrants to remain in Mexico.

United States.title: FBI's search of Trump's estate sparks outrage.
United States.summary: The FBI's warrantless search of former President Trump's Mar-a-Lago estate has sparked outrage among Republicans, raising concerns about presidential immunity and the potential for future political persecution.

United States.title: Major US airlines face possible staff shortages as summer travel surges.
United States.summary: As summer travel surges, major US airlines such as American Airlines, Delta Air Lines, and United Airlines are facing possible staff shortages due to flight delays, cancellations, and the ongoing labour dispute with their pilots.

South Korea.title: Protesters set fire to North Korean propaganda billboards in South Gyeongsang Province
South Korea.summary: South Korea's anti-Pyongyang activist group, who call themselves 'Our Republic, Our Life, Our Nationalism, Our Democracy', were accused of setting fire to North Korean propaganda billboards in the South Gyeongsang Province on August 1st.

South Korea.title: South Korea raises interest rates to combat inflation
South Korea.summary: On 11th of August, the Bank of Korea increased its benchmark interest rate to 3.75% in an effort to keep a lid on high inflation. The policy is expected to affect the country's economy and the lives of its citizens.

South Korea.title: North Korea fires missile over Japan, South Korea urges calm
South Korea.summary: Last week, North Korea fired a missile over Japan's northern island of Hokkaido. South Korea has since urged its citizens to remain calm and said it will continue to work with the international community to address the situation.

Japan.title: Japan's Constitutional Panel Reiterates Need for Emergency Powers
Japan.summary: Japan's advisory panel on its post-war constitution reiterated the need for emergency powers, amid ongoing discussions on the country's security laws. This issue has long been a contentious topic in Japan, with concerns about the impact on human rights.

Japan.title: Abe's Suspicions Over China-Japan Relations Intensify
Japan.summary: As tensions between China and Japan escalate over disputed islands, Shinzo Abe's suspicions over Beijing's intentions are intensifying, with some analysts suggesting that China may be planning to make a move on the islands in the coming days.

Japan.title: Japanese Government Seeks to Revamp National Security Laws
Japan.summary: The Japanese government has submitted a bill to the parliament to revamp the country's national security laws, amid growing concerns about the threat posed by North Korea and China. The proposed changes aim to strengthen Tokyo's security posture and bolster its alliances with the US and other nations.
